title: Mountain Temple Bell Chronicle
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk Jingkong（Bell monk Jingkong in his fifties, shaved gray-blue scalp, earth-yellow robe, coarse hemp wrist wraps, deep calluses on the palms, calm manner） climbs the wooden ladder into the belfry inner hall（Mountain temple belfry inner hall, wooden lattice windows on four sides, bronze morning bell hung at center, worn cushions on the floor, incense-ash smell year-round） and tightens his coarse hemp wrist wraps.
A row of five eternal oil lamps（A row of five eternal oil lamps hung on the belfry beam, glass shades polished, wicks trimmed neat） hangs in the belfry inner hall; Jingkong polishes each one.
Two eave wind bells（Two bronze eave wind bells hung at the eaves corner, chiming lightly when the wind rises） hang by the door side; Jingkong reaches out and lets them chime lightly.
Jingkong tip-toes to check whether lotus-petal patterns on the bronze morning bell outer wall have gathered ash.
Jingkong looks out toward the valley cloud sea beyond the temple front stone flat.

The intact bronze morning bell（A bronze morning bell taller than a man, lip intact, lotus-petal patterns cast on the outer wall, hung under the belfry beam） hangs under the beam; oil-lamp light flows lightly on the lip.
Jingkong adds this morning's and afternoon's strike hours on the evening-duty plaque.
Jingkong removes and rewraps the wrist wraps, confirming the knot holds.
Jingkong sorts scattered ash scoops and realigns them for morning and evening duty.
Jingkong sits on a belfry cushion and rubs his aching neck and shoulders.

Jingkong opens the duty booklet（A yellow-paper thread-bound duty booklet recording daily strike counts and hours, cover clean） and writes strike counts and aftertone length in dawn-bell and dusk-bell columns.
Beside today's column Jingkong draws small lotus circles marking a dull morning-bell aftertone.
Jingkong closes the duty booklet and presses it under a wooden ruler on the altar left so ash cannot drift in.
Reflection from the bronze morning bell sweeps Jingkong's profile.
Jingkong matches the bronze morning bell and circles a dull lotus petal on the lip with vermilion ink.
Jingkong returns ash scoop and wrist wraps to a wood box so they will not snag the rope when striking.

On the temple front stone flat（Temple front stone flat, moss in the seams, view of valley cloud seas, incense visitors at dawn and dusk） at dawn, Jingkong greets young Acheng（Young Acheng: a lean novice apprentice around fifteen, turmeric monk sock ties at the ankles, bright stubborn eyes） bringing the cedar striking beam（A long thick cedar striking beam, both ends wrapped in old cotton, suspension rope intact, able to strike the bell lip steadily）.
Acheng sets the cedar striking beam in place and pats dust from his clothes.
Jingkong points to three altar bronze bowls（Three small bronze bowls on the incense altar, same size, lightly tapped before and after duty） and teaches Acheng their places and uses.
Acheng crouches at the temple front stone flat edge listening to the three bronze bowls' aftertones.
Jingkong explains to Acheng the rules: palms together before striking, half-step back, listen to the aftertone.
Acheng looks back at the intact cedar striking beam, eyes full of longing.
Jingkong has Acheng grip the cedar striking beam cotton end and practice stop-then-strike rhythm.
Acheng tightens the turmeric monk sock ties and silently counts three strike measures Jingkong speaks.

In the sutra-store narrow passage（A narrow passage to the sutra storehouse, tall scripture cabinets on both sides, oil lamps stretching shadows long）, Ache（Ache whose face and build closely match Acheng's, but wearing an amber prayer-bead brooch, swaggering and eager to strike first） with an amber prayer-bead brooch glances back from the dark.
Ache walks slowly through the sutra-store narrow passage with a swaggering look.
Ache brushes past a passerby; the amber prayer-bead brooch sways lightly.
Ache stops at the passage mouth and pickily critiques the sutra-store swap-card handwriting.
Ache kicks a clump of incense ash to the wall corner.
Ache turns into a side door at the passage end and leaves.
On the temple front stone flat, Acheng and Ache stand side by side—one with turmeric monk sock ties, one with an amber prayer-bead brooch.
Acheng hands Ache a picked-up bronze-bowl mallet head; they meet eyes with different looks.
Ache smooths Acheng's turmeric monk sock ties, then deliberately clicks his amber prayer-bead brooch.
Acheng and Ache walk slowly along the temple front stone flat edge; shadows overlap then split.
Acheng looks down checking evening strike rhythm; Ache looks about.
Acheng and Ache part at the temple front stone flat mouth, each walking opposite ways.
Months later at night, Jingkong keeps watch alone in the belfry inner hall; the bronze morning bell waits quietly.

Jingkong opens the duty booklet（The same duty booklet stained by incense ash, cover gray, writing abraded by ash grit, a crumpled blotting sheet tucked inside） and finds it already incense-ash stained, writing damaged.
Jingkong wipes dust and grime from the bronze morning bell surface.
Jingkong looks out toward night beyond the temple front stone flat.
Lamplight slowly moves across the bronze morning bell.
Jingkong slips blotting paper into the stained duty booklet, sighs, and turns out the light.
Jingkong wipes the bronze morning bell rim in the belfry inner hall.
Jingkong updates the day's note on the wall.
Jingkong rearranges tools by number.
Jingkong checks yesterday's records against the duty booklet.
In the afternoon Jingkong takes an outside call, brow faintly furrowed.
Jingkong writes deferred items on a sticky note and posts it in plain view.
Jingkong pulls spare materials aside and sorts them.
At dusk Jingkong turns off extra lamps, leaving only the central one on the bronze morning bell.
Jingkong spreads tracing paper or a comparison chart in the belfry inner hall.
Jingkong marks spots needing reinforcement with color dots.
Jingkong fixes the paper edges to stop curling.
Jingkong compares the already-stained duty booklet, straining to read old numbers.
Jingkong sets drinks far away for fear of another splash on the duty booklet.
Jingkong lists three proposed adjustments on the wall.
Noise outside; Jingkong looks up and listens a moment.
Jingkong restrings the tags with thin cord.
On inspection day Jingkong walks onto the temple front stone flat.
Jingkong carefully tests whether ground or railings are secure.
Jingkong notes spots that need repair.
Jingkong shines a flashlight into dim corners.
Jingkong briefly talks with a passing staffer.
Jingkong skirts piled clutter and goes around to the other side.
Jingkong records size changes with a tape or by eye.
Jingkong writes results on a cuff sticky note.
At daybreak Jingkong patrols the temple front stone flat; the cedar striking beam sits in place.
Jingkong crouches to check the cedar striking beam rope knots and cotton-end wear.
Jingkong walks to the incense altar; those three altar bronze bowls still sit on wood rests in morning-noon-evening order.

A pilgrim lifts a tourist blessing mallet（A tourist blessing mallet, shaped somewhat like a striker but short, handle carved with Joyful Offering） before the belfry—that short blessing mallet has neither suspension rope nor old cotton ends, nothing like the cedar striking beam.
Jingkong stands on the temple front stone flat and notes moss change in stone seams before the belfry on the patrol plaque.
Jingkong rewinds the cedar striking beam rope through the beam ring and tightens it.
Jingkong confirms again that none of the three altar bronze bowls is missing and mallet heads have not shifted.
Jingkong writes the patrol date on a small wood tag by the altar.
On the eve of disaster Jingkong stores all by-window materials into cabinets.
Jingkong covers the bronze morning bell with protective cloth.
Jingkong checks whether the duty booklet is in a dry drawer.
Jingkong tightens bottle caps and valves and moves them high.
A strange noise afar; lights in the belfry inner hall flicker once.
Jingkong tidies the cables of the five eternal oil lamps.
Jingkong drafts a notice: Closed tomorrow.
Jingkong listens whether the two eave wind bells are chiming in the wind.
A storm rises suddenly; belfry lattice windows shake hard; the suspension rope swings violently.
A draft lifts scripture banners; the striking beam swings left and right hard.
Thunder cracks; a lengthwise crack bursts on the bronze morning bell（The same bronze morning bell with a lengthwise crack, lip chipped, aftertone dull and incomplete）; the aftertone goes dull.
On the beam, the cedar striking beam still hangs in midair jolting hard.

One hard swing snaps the cedar striking beam（The cedar striking beam snapped in the middle, cotton ends frayed, only wreckage hanging askew in midair） in the middle; cotton ends fray—only askew wreckage left.
In the belfry Jingkong lunges for the rope and fiercely steadies the cracked bronze morning bell.
Jingkong's right wrist is whipped by the broken rope; blood seeps into white cloth; he still guards the bell lip.
The cracked bronze morning bell sways slowly in the wind.
The day after the disaster, Jingkong stands in the belfry inner hall staring at the already-cracked bronze morning bell.
Jingkong traces the damage on the bronze morning bell with a finger, face dark.
Jingkong notes the date the cedar striking beam was destroyed on the belfry repair plaque.
An old photo of the cedar striking beam with intact cotton ends is still nailed to the wall; Jingkong gazes long.
Jingkong turns up one of the five eternal oil lamps and sits alone in the light patch.
The cracked bronze morning bell still hangs under the beam; the lip chip is shocking.
Jingkong changes the blood-seeping bandage and keeps clearing the site.
Jingkong re-covers with protective cloth, fearing the damage will spread.
In cleanup week Jingkong packs shards into cardboard boxes.
Jingkong submits a funding request for repair materials.
Jingkong still comes to the belfry inner hall every day, staring at the damaged bronze morning bell.
Jingkong pencils still-readable details.
Jingkong turns the stained duty booklet to a blank page and switches to logging funding progress.
Acheng is on leave; only Jingkong's footsteps remain in the belfry inner hall.
Jingkong habitually touches the empty place where the cedar striking beam used to rest.
Jingkong lists materials needed for repair on the wall.
Weeks later Jingkong brings a bell caster, lays out copper strips and a fine file, and begins repairing the bronze morning bell.

Jingkong takes out a pocket bronze bell ornament（A pocket bronze bell ornament shaped like a small bell but without lotus-petal patterns, wood base）—like a shrunk bell body but without lotus-petal patterns and without a knob that can hang from a beam.
Jingkong clears ash along the crack, embeds copper strips, then files the lip chip smooth.

The last copper embed is filed smooth; the bronze morning bell（After repair the bronze morning bell crack is copper-filled smooth, but a shallow mend mark remains on the outer wall, distinct from the original intact state） repair is done, leaving a shallow mend mark at the crack.
When the repaired bronze morning bell is lightly struck the aftertone rounds again; Jingkong looks at it with relief.
Jingkong pushes the pocket bronze bell ornament aside, leaving only the true bronze morning bell centered under the beam.
The belfry inner hall falls quiet again; the repaired bronze morning bell holds the center alone.

A dharma-assembly line pushes a vermilion dharma drum cart（A vermilion dharma-assembly drum cart, drum face wide and round with no bell lip, Dharma Assembly lettered on the side）—wide round drum face, no suspension rope, nothing like the long-destroyed cedar striking beam.

Prefecture steward Huiming（Prefecture steward Huiming whose build somewhat resembles Jingkong's, brown robe, key ring on the shoulder, monk's hat instead of wrist-wrap marks） walks onto the temple front stone flat and talks shoulder to shoulder with Jingkong; their builds are alike.
Prefecture steward Huiming points at the vermilion dharma drum cart and tells Jingkong the cart only uses the front flat, never the belfry strike line.
The vermilion dharma drum cart leaves; Jingkong alone watches it from the temple front stone flat.
The vermilion dharma drum cart pauses briefly afar, then moves on.
Before leaving, Prefecture steward Huiming pats Jingkong's shoulder; the key ring flashes under the lamp.

Novice Xiao Jing（Novice Xiao Jing who at a glance resembles young Acheng, light-gray sock ties rather than turmeric monk sock ties, shy unfamiliar eyes） arrives on the temple front stone flat; at a glance he looks somewhat like young Acheng.
Novice Xiao Jing tries pulling the striking beam, but Jingkong shakes his head—he is not Acheng after all.
Novice Xiao Jing shyly asks when evening bells strike; Jingkong answers briefly and sends him to wipe bronze bowls by the altar.
Jingkong alone stands on the temple front stone flat staring at the empty place where the cedar striking beam used to rest.
In the first ten days after repair Jingkong checks the bronze morning bell every dawn first.
Jingkong writes new records on blank pages of the stained duty booklet.
Jingkong refuses to set dangerous items near the edge again.
Jingkong checks notice copy with the outside.
Jingkong practices steadier handling in the belfry inner hall.
Afternoon light falls on the repaired bronze morning bell.
Jingkong polishes the eave wind bells bright but does not strike them yet.
Jingkong receives Acheng's postcard and presses it under a lamp base unopened.
Jingkong realigns cushion directions in the belfry inner hall.
Jingkong wipes new incense ash from the bronze morning bell outer wall.
Jingkong dog-ears a blank duty-booklet page for tomorrow's continuation.
Jingkong listens to the eave wind bells and checks evening duty time.
Jingkong looks once at the valley cloud sea from the stone-flat end.
At year-end closing Jingkong binds the year's papers by month.
Jingkong puts the stained duty booklet alone into an archive pouch.
Jingkong prints before-and-after repair photos and clips them into the archive.
Jingkong clears the desk, leaving only necessary tools and one lamp.
Jingkong oils key tools against rust.
Jingkong signs a date beside the bronze morning bell repair mark.
Weather turns cold outside; heating or stove fire ticks lightly in the belfry inner hall.
Jingkong finishes the annual summary; the cover holds only a short theme.

Years later at dusk, still-scarred heavy-stepping Jingkong（The same Jingkong weary and injured: robe corner torn, right wrist wrapped in white cloth, still in coarse hemp wraps, heavy steps） leans on a wooden staff at the abandoned side-hall ruins（Abandoned side-hall ruins, half walls left, peeling stone steps, weeds thrusting from brick seams）.
Jingkong looks up at the abandoned side-hall ruins remnants, gaze far away.
By the abandoned side-hall ruins, those two eave wind bells are brought back and hung; they chime lightly in the wind.
Jingkong presses his palm to the cold remnant-wall bricks, as if saying goodbye.
Jingkong slowly sits to catch his breath a moment.
The two eave wind bells chime lightly again; Jingkong closes his eyes to listen, as if hearing evening duty bells of old.
Jingkong still returns to the belfry inner hall daily, but sits longer watching the bronze morning bell.
Jingkong leans his staff by the door; he moves slower than before.
Jingkong lets a young aide write notes; he only checks.
Jingkong photographs the repaired bronze morning bell for distant Acheng.
Jingkong writes Handover on the stained duty-booklet last page but does not sign.
Jingkong refuses hospital and insists on sitting at the abandoned side-hall ruins each week.
Jingkong wipes a draft of the bluestone merit stele.
At night only one lamp remains in the belfry inner hall; Jingkong dozes in the light circle.

By day, adult Acheng（Adult Acheng: a solid-shouldered successor bell-striker in his twenties, still in turmeric monk sock ties, steady eyes） returns along the abandoned side-hall ruins and hurries toward the remnants.
Acheng reunites with heavy-stepping Jingkong at the abandoned side-hall ruins; they embrace.
By the bed in the belfry inner hall, Acheng holds Jingkong's withered hand.
Jingkong（Jingkong has retired from duty; only his old earth-yellow robe and duty plaque remain in the belfry—he himself no longer appears）'s breath fades; at last he closes his eyes and dies.
Acheng stands long at the abandoned side-hall ruins; tears fall on the ground.
Acheng wraps Jingkong's coarse hemp wrist wraps onto his own wrist.
Jingkong's old coat still hangs behind the belfry inner hall door; Acheng reaches out and gently strokes it.

By the abandoned side-hall ruins, adult Acheng stands before the newly nailed bluestone merit stele（A bluestone merit stele nailed to the side-hall remnant wall, carved with Jingkong and the year, moss on the edges）.
Acheng's fingertip traces Jingkong's name carved on the bluestone merit stele.
Acheng sets a white chrysanthemum at the lower edge of the bluestone merit stele.
Wind passes the abandoned side-hall ruins; Acheng softly speaks the year on the plaque.

Disguised adult Ache（After a change of look Ache still wears the amber prayer-bead brooch, now also a short gray kasaya, expression deeper） arrives and embraces Acheng tightly at the abandoned side-hall ruins.
Acheng and Ache stand side by side by the bluestone merit stele—one quiet-eyed, one deep-faced.
Ache touches his amber prayer-bead brooch, then looks at the coarse hemp wrist wraps on Acheng's wrist.
They look at each other in silence, faces similar yet different.
Acheng and Ache walk toward the end together; shadows merge into one.
The shot returns years—that youth on the stone flat in turmeric monk sock ties looking up at the belfry appears again.
The opening moment returns—in the belfry, a bronze great bell cast with lotus-petal patterns is struck for the first time.
Flash back to the sutra-store narrow passage that year—a figure with an amber prayer-bead brooch hurrying to cut the path flashes past.
Again that row of five old lamps on the belfry beam.
Back to that mossy temple-front stone flat of first meeting; pilgrim footsteps as before.
Pages turn—that yellow-paper thread-bound booklet still free of incense ash, filled with strike hours, appears again.
Acheng reopens the already incense-ash-stained duty booklet and walks into the belfry inner hall.
On the belfry inner hall table, those three altar bronze bowls still sit neat.
Acheng takes over watch of the bronze morning bell; the repair mark is clear under the light.
Acheng turns up the five eternal oil lamps; light fills the space again.
Acheng stands straight before the repaired bronze morning bell, checking evening strike hours as Jingkong once did.
